title: Science Card
description:
Canonical, runtime-neutral definition of a Squad Science Card: a durable record of a research question moving through phases (QUESTION -> DIVERGE -> ORIENT -> HYPOTHESIZE -> DERIVE -> ATTACK -> SIMULATE -> EXPERIMENT -> REPLICATE -> SUPPORTED | FALSIFIED | INCONCLUSIVE, with LEARN -> PIVOT loops and an ABANDONED escape hatch), carrying typed evidence and a full transition history. This file has no Claude- or Codex-specific fields and no fields specific to any single agent runtime — `persona` is a plain string identifying whichever agent or human acted.

Schema ownership: this file is the canonical Science Card schema for the cross-repo effort tracked by squad#20 (companion issues rjwalters/loom#6109 and rjwalters/lean-genius#43705). Other repos should vendor a copy with a comment noting the `$id`/`version` it was copied from (or otherwise reference this file), not independently redefine the shape. Bump `version` (semver) on any breaking change to this shape so vendored copies can detect drift.

question.description: The research question this card investigates.

phase.description: Current phase in the transition graph.

claim_kind.description: Whether reaching SUPPORTED requires empirical evidence (experiment/observation) or is satisfiable by formal evidence alone (derivation/formal-check). Keeps evidence-level 'verified' distinct from card-level 'SUPPORTED': a verified derivation never alone satisfies an empirical claim.

origin_contributors.description: Personas (agents or humans) credited with originating this card.

changed_assumptions.description: Assumptions this card revises relative to prior work.

math_model.description: Math or model statement, if any.

discriminating_prediction.description: The prediction that discriminates this hypothesis from the standard/null one.

decisive_falsifier.description: What observation/result would decisively falsify this card's claim.

cheapest_test.description: The cheapest available test that could move this card forward.

provenance.description: Where this evidence came from — non-empty, required.
